title: Block Puzzle Blitz
shortDescription: Drag colourful blocks onto an 8x8 board and fill whole rows or columns to clear them. Chain clears on back-to-back moves for big combo points, and keep going until nothing fits.
howToPlay: Drag one of the three blocks in your tray onto the board and let go to drop it. Fill every square in a row or a column to clear that line. When all three blocks are placed you get a new set. Clearing lines on consecutive moves builds a combo multiplier. The game ends when none of your remaining blocks fits anywhere on the board.
about: Block Puzzle Blitz is a relaxing but surprisingly tactical block puzzle game. There is no timer and no falling pieces: you choose where every block goes, so each game is about planning ahead and keeping enough open space for whatever shape comes next.

Points come from every square you place, with bigger rewards for clearing several lines at once and for clearing on back-to-back moves. Blocks that no longer fit anywhere fade out in your tray, so you can always see how close you are to running out of room.
tips: Keep at least one full row or column empty so a long 1x5 bar always has somewhere to go.
Place the awkward 3x3 square early while the board still has room for it.
Clearing a row and a column with one block scores far more than clearing them separately.
Look at all three tray pieces before placing the first one, and plan where each will fit.

faq.q: How do combos work in Block Puzzle Blitz?
faq.a: Every time you clear at least one line on consecutive placements, your combo grows and each clear is worth an extra 10 points per combo step. Placing a block that clears nothing resets the combo.

faq.q: When does the game end?
faq.a: The game ends when none of the blocks left in your tray can fit anywhere on the board. Faded blocks in the tray are the ones that no longer fit.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Mine Hunt
shortDescription: The classic mine-clearing logic puzzle. Read the numbers, flag the hidden mines and open every safe square on Easy, Medium or Hard boards. Your first tap is always safe.
howToPlay: Click or tap a square to open it. A number tells you how many of the eight squares around it hide a mine. Right-click or long-press a square to plant a flag where you are sure a mine is, or switch on Flag mode in the top bar. Tap an opened number that already has the right number of flags around it to open all of its other neighbours at once. Open every safe square to win.
about: Mine Hunt is a fresh take on the mine-clearing puzzle that has been a favourite on computers for decades. Every board is pure logic: the numbers always contain enough information to make progress, and the fun is in spotting the patterns that tell you exactly where the mines are.

Choose Easy (9x9, 10 mines) for a quick game, Medium (12x12, 24 mines) for a proper challenge, or Hard (16x16, 48 mines) for a long session. Your best time is saved separately for each difficulty, and your first tap always opens a safe area.
tips: A 1 touching only one unopened square means that square is a mine, so flag it.
Look for the 1-2-1 pattern along a wall: the mines sit next to the two 1s.
Tapping a satisfied number to open its neighbours saves a lot of time on bigger boards.
If you are truly stuck, guess in a corner. Corners have fewer neighbours, so they are less likely to set off a chain.

faq.q: Is the first click in Mine Hunt always safe?
faq.a: Yes. Mines are placed after your first tap and never in the 3x3 area around it, so the first move always opens up part of the board.

faq.q: How do I flag a mine on a phone?
faq.a: Long-press a square, or turn on Flag mode in the top bar so a normal tap plants a flag instead of opening the square.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Klondike Solitaire
shortDescription: Classic Klondike solitaire with Draw 1 and Draw 3 modes. Drag cards or tap to auto-move, undo as often as you like, and let auto-finish wrap up the game once every card is face up.
howToPlay: Move all 52 cards onto the four foundations at the top right, building each one up by suit from Ace to King. In the seven columns below, build down in alternating colours (a red 6 on a black 7). Only a King can move into an empty column. Tap the deck to deal new cards. Drag a card or a run of cards to move it, or tap a card to send it to the best legal spot. Use Undo to take back moves.
about: Klondike Solitaire is the card game most people simply call solitaire. This version keeps the rules you know and adds the comforts that make it quick to play in a browser: tap-to-move, unlimited undo, and an automatic finish once the game is effectively won.

Play Draw 1 for a relaxed game you can usually win, or switch to Draw 3 for the tougher traditional challenge. Your best time and move count are saved for each mode, so there is always a record to beat.
tips: Turning over face-down cards in the columns matters more than anything else, so work on the tallest columns first.
Do not rush cards onto the foundations if you still need them to hold other cards in the columns.
Only empty a column when you have a King ready to move into it.
In Draw 3, try to keep the deck order changing by playing cards from the waste whenever you can.

faq.q: What is the difference between Draw 1 and Draw 3?
faq.a: In Draw 1 you turn over one card from the deck at a time and can play every card. In Draw 3 you turn over three and can only play the top one, which makes the game much harder.

faq.q: Can I undo moves in Klondike Solitaire?
faq.a: Yes. Use the Undo button in the top bar or press Ctrl+Z as many times as you like.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Turf Takeover
shortDescription: An io-style territory battle. Leave your zone to draw a trail, loop back home to claim everything inside, and cut across rival trails to knock them out before they take the map.
howToPlay: Steer with the arrow keys or WASD, or swipe on a touchscreen. While you are outside your own colour you leave a trail behind you. Return to your zone to turn the whole enclosed area into your territory, including land owned by bots. Drive across a rival's trail to knock them out, but never touch your own trail and keep your trail safe from rivals, or you are out.
about: Turf Takeover is a fast territory-capture game inspired by the io games that took over school breaks and lunch hours. You start with a small patch of the map and five computer rivals who want the same land.

Every trip outside your zone is a gamble: a bigger loop claims more ground but leaves your trail exposed for longer. Your score is the largest share of the map you held during the run, and knocked-out rivals respawn so the competition never stops.
tips: Short, quick loops close to home are the safest way to grow early.
Rivals are most vulnerable when they are far from home with a long trail behind them.
Use the minimap in the corner to spot open, unclaimed ground.
Claiming land a rival is standing in will not knock them out, but cutting their trail will.

faq.q: How do I claim territory in Turf Takeover?
faq.a: Leave your coloured zone, draw a loop with your trail, and return to your zone. Everything inside the loop becomes yours.

faq.q: What knocks you out?
faq.a: Touching your own trail, hitting the edge of the map, or a rival crossing your trail while you are outside your zone.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Checkmate Chess
shortDescription: Play full-rules chess against the computer on Easy, Normal or Hard. Castling, en passant and promotion are all in, with move hints, last-move highlights and undo.
howToPlay: You play the white pieces. Tap or click one of your pieces to see the squares it can move to, then tap a highlighted square to make the move. The computer replies straight away. Pawns that reach the far side become queens. Use Undo to take back your last move, and switch between Easy, Normal and Hard from the top bar.
about: Checkmate Chess gives you a complete game of chess in a browser tab, with every official rule including castling, en passant, promotion, stalemate and the 50-move rule. Legal moves are highlighted, so it is a friendly way to learn as well as to practise.

The computer opponent comes in three strengths. Easy makes the occasional mistake and is great for beginners, Normal punishes loose pieces, and Hard looks several moves deep and searches capture sequences. Your wins against each level are counted on your device.
tips: Control the centre early with your e and d pawns and develop knights before bishops.
Castle in the first ten moves to keep your king safe.
Before every move, check whether any of your pieces are undefended.
On Hard, avoid trading pieces when you are behind; look for forks and pins instead.

faq.q: Does Checkmate Chess follow the official rules?
faq.a: Yes. Castling, en passant, pawn promotion, check, checkmate, stalemate, the 50-move rule and draws by insufficient material are all supported. Pawns always promote to a queen.

faq.q: How strong is the Hard computer?
faq.a: Hard searches three moves ahead and then follows capture sequences, so it rarely leaves pieces hanging. It is a solid challenge for casual and club-level players.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Tower Rush Defense
shortDescription: Build and upgrade towers along a winding road to stop waves of monsters reaching your castle gate. Armoured brutes arrive from wave five and a boss every ten waves.
howToPlay: Tap or click a + pad beside the road to build a tower for 60 gold, and tap an existing tower to upgrade it (up to level 3). Towers fire automatically at the monster furthest along the road. Kills earn gold and every cleared wave pays a bonus. Press N to call the next wave early.
about: Tower Rush Defense is a compact tower defence game that is easy to start and surprisingly deep. Monsters follow a winding road towards your castle, and your only weapons are the towers you build on the pads beside it.

Each upgrade increases a tower's range, fire rate and damage, so deciding between building new towers and upgrading existing ones is the heart of the game. Waves grow larger and tougher, with armoured brutes from wave five and a powerful boss every ten waves.
tips: Build your first towers near the corners, where they can cover two stretches of road.
Upgrading one tower is often stronger than building two weak ones.
Save some gold before every tenth wave for the boss.
A boss reaching the gate costs five lives, so stack firepower near the end of the road.

faq.q: How do I upgrade towers in Tower Rush Defense?
faq.a: Tap a tower you have already built. Each upgrade costs more gold but boosts range, speed and damage, up to level 3.

faq.q: What happens when monsters reach the gate?
faq.a: You lose a life for each one, or five for a boss. The game ends when you run out of lives.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Tank Wars
shortDescription: Turn-based artillery on rolling hills. Set your angle and power, read the wind, and lob shells at the enemy tank — every explosion carves a crater in the ground.
howToPlay: On your turn, use ← → to change the barrel angle and ↑ ↓ to set power, then press Space to fire. On a touchscreen or with a mouse, drag back from your tank like a slingshot and release to shoot. Check the wind arrow at the top before every shot.
about: Tank Wars is a classic turn-based artillery game. You and an enemy tank sit on opposite hills and take turns firing shells, adjusting angle and power to account for gravity and a wind that changes every turn.

Every explosion destroys part of the landscape, so the battlefield changes as the duel goes on. Beat the bot and the next one aims more accurately, which turns a casual game into a real test of judgement over a streak of wins.
tips: Make one change at a time — adjust either angle or power after a miss, not both.
Strong wind matters most on high, slow arcs; flatter shots are less affected.
Craters can shelter your tank, but they can also trap shells aimed at you.
Watch where the enemy's shells land to judge the wind for your next shot.

faq.q: How does the wind work in Tank Wars?
faq.a: Wind pushes shells left or right while they fly. Its strength and direction are shown at the top of the screen and change slightly every turn.

faq.q: Does the bot get harder?
faq.a: Yes. Each round you win makes the next enemy aim more accurately.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Sky Hopper
shortDescription: Bounce higher and higher on floating platforms. Steer the hopper left and right, catch springs for big launches, and watch out for platforms that slide away or crumble under your feet.
howToPlay: The hopper jumps automatically every time it lands — you only steer. Use ← → or A and D on a keyboard, or hold the left or right half of the screen on a phone. Moving off one side of the screen brings you back on the other.
about: Sky Hopper is an endless vertical jumping game inspired by classic doodle-style climbers. Your little hopper bounces automatically, so the entire game is about steering: lining up the next platform, catching springs and avoiding traps as you climb into the sky.

Green platforms are safe, blue ones slide back and forth, and cracked brown ones break the moment you touch them. Springs launch you far above the screen. The higher you climb, the bigger the gaps and the trickier the platforms become.
tips: Aim for the middle of platforms so a small misjudgement doesn't send you past the edge.
Use screen wrapping — sometimes the closest platform is on the other side.
Cracked platforms break instantly; treat them as background, not as steps.
Springs are worth a detour, since one launch can be worth several ordinary jumps.

faq.q: How do I control Sky Hopper on a phone?
faq.a: Hold your finger on the left half of the screen to move left and on the right half to move right.

faq.q: What do the different platforms do?
faq.a: Green platforms are solid, blue ones move sideways, brown cracked ones break when you land, and springs launch you much higher.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Chicken Road Cross
shortDescription: Help a brave chicken hop across busy roads and rushing rivers. Dodge cars, ride the logs, and keep moving — the screen creeps forward whether you are ready or not.
howToPlay: Arrow keys or WASD hop one tile at a time; on a phone, tap to hop forward or swipe in any direction. Cars on the roads end the run, water does too unless you are standing on a log, and the camera keeps creeping up the screen — fall off the bottom and you are left behind.
about: Chicken Road Cross is an endless lane-hopping arcade game in the spirit of classic road-crossing games. Every row is grass, road or river, and each one asks something different: wait for a gap in traffic, time a jump onto a drifting log, or weave between trees on the grass.

The world is generated as you go, so no two runs are the same, and traffic gets faster the further you get. Every row you reach is a point — and because the screen slowly moves on its own, standing still is never safe for long.
tips: Watch the lane after the next one, not just the one in front of you.
On rivers, hop on to a log early and ride it while you plan your next jump.
Logs carry you sideways — don't let one drift you off the edge of the screen.
Use grass rows as resting spots, but don't rest so long the screen catches up.

faq.q: How do you score in Chicken Road Cross?
faq.a: You score one point for every new row you reach. Your best score is saved in your browser.

faq.q: Can the chicken swim?
faq.a: No. On river rows you must land on a log; touching the water ends the run.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Pixel Dash
shortDescription: An endless runner with two inputs and no brakes. Jump the blocks and the gaps, duck under the saw blades, and see how far you get before it outruns your reflexes.
howToPlay: Space or a tap jumps; hold ↓ (or hold a finger on the lower third of the screen) to duck. Blocks and gaps you jump, saw blades you duck under — a blade sits too low to jump and too high to run through.
about: Pixel Dash is a fast endless runner built around just two moves. Your runner never stops, so every second is a decision: jump the block, clear the gap, or drop low before a saw blade sweeps through at head height.

The course is generated as you go and the pace climbs the further you get, which keeps every run short, tense and easy to restart. It is the kind of game you play for thirty seconds and then, somehow, for twenty minutes.
tips: Watch the height of each hazard, not just its position — saw blades are always a duck, never a jump.
Jump a fraction late on blocks; early jumps land you on top of the next obstacle.
On a phone, rest a thumb on the lower third of the screen so ducking is instant.
Your best runs come from rhythm — stop reacting to single obstacles and read the next two.

faq.q: How do you duck in Pixel Dash?
faq.a: Hold the down arrow on a keyboard, or hold a finger on the lower third of the screen on a phone or tablet.

faq.q: Does Pixel Dash get harder?
faq.a: Yes. The speed increases steadily with distance, so obstacles arrive closer together the longer you survive.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Stack Tower Rush
shortDescription: Tap at exactly the right moment to drop each block dead centre. Perfect stacks stay wide, sloppy ones shave your tower down to a toothpick.
howToPlay: One input: Space or a tap drops the sliding block. Anything hanging over the edge is sliced off and the next block is that much narrower, so land them centred. A perfect drop is forgiven entirely and widens your margin back.
about: Stack Tower Rush is a one-button timing game. A block slides back and forth above your tower and you drop it with a single tap — land it centred and the tower stays wide, miss and the overhang is sliced away for good.

Every mistake makes the next drop harder because there is less tower to land on, while a perfect drop restores some of the width you lost. It is a pure test of timing and nerve, and runs perfectly on a school Chromebook.
tips: Tap on the rhythm of the slide, not when the block looks lined up — your reaction delay is part of the timing.
Chase perfect drops early, while the tower is wide; they rebuild margin you will need later.
If the block speeds up, shorten your look-ahead and focus only on the near edge.
Take a breath after a bad drop — players lose more towers rushing the recovery than the mistake itself.

faq.q: What counts as a perfect drop?
faq.a: A block that lands almost exactly on top of the one below. Perfect drops cut nothing off and widen your margin back.

faq.q: What ends a run?
faq.a: Missing the tower completely. Each sloppy drop shrinks the tower until there is nothing left to land on.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Drift Alley
shortDescription: Hold one key to drift, release to grip. Slide through an apex to grow your chain, arrive straight and lose it, and clip a wall to end the run.
howToPlay: ←→ steers, Space holds a drift; on a phone, hold anywhere and slide left or right. Sliding through a corner builds your chain — arrive straight and you lose it, clip a wall and the run is over.
about: Drift Alley is an arcade drifting game where the whole skill is knowing when to let the back end go. Hold to slide, release to grip, and string corners together to grow a drift chain that multiplies your score.
Arrive at a corner straight and your chain resets; touch a wall and the run ends. It rewards smooth, committed lines over raw speed, which makes it easy to learn and surprisingly hard to master.
tips: Start the drift before the corner, not in it — late slides send you wide into the wall.
Release early to straighten out; holding too long is the most common way to clip the outside.
Small steering inputs keep the chain alive better than big corrections.
Learn one stretch of track at a time and repeat it until the line feels automatic.

faq.q: How do I drift on mobile?
faq.a: Hold anywhere on the screen to drift and slide your finger left or right to steer. Lift your finger to grip again.

faq.q: How do drift chains work?
faq.a: Each corner you slide through adds to your chain and raises the score multiplier. Arriving at a corner without drifting breaks the chain.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Neon Snake
shortDescription: The classic snake loop with a glow-up: speed ramps every ten pellets, and the lit gap in the middle of each wall wraps you across — everything else is solid.
howToPlay: Arrows, WASD or a swipe turns. Speed steps up every ten pellets. Only the lit gap in the middle of each wall wraps you through to the other side — the rest of the wall, and your own tail, ends the run.
about: Neon Snake is the classic snake game with a glowing makeover and one important twist. Eat pellets to grow, avoid your own tail, and use the lit gap in the centre of each wall to wrap across to the other side of the board.

The snake speeds up every ten pellets, so the calm opening quickly turns into a reflex test. Because only the gaps wrap, the walls still matter — every route through the board has to be planned around them.
tips: Use the wall gaps to escape when your tail starts boxing you in.
Keep long, sweeping paths along the edges rather than zig-zagging through the middle.
Plan your next two turns before the speed steps up at each ten-pellet mark.
Swipes register best when short and decisive on a touchscreen.

faq.q: Can I go through the walls in Neon Snake?
faq.a: Only through the glowing gap in the middle of each wall. Hitting any other part of the wall ends the run.

faq.q: When does the snake get faster?
faq.a: The speed steps up every time you eat ten pellets.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Hoop Streak
shortDescription: Drag, release, sink the shot, keep the streak alive. You get sixty seconds, and the hoop starts sliding at ten baskets — then stops being polite at twenty-five.
howToPlay: Drag away from the ball and let go — the direction sets the arc, the distance sets the power. Or use ←→ for angle, ↑↓ for power, Space to shoot. Sixty seconds; nothing but net pays a bonus and every make in a row is worth more than the last.
about: Hoop Streak is a sixty-second basketball shooting game. Drag back from the ball to set the angle and power, release, and try to keep your streak alive — every basket in a row is worth more than the last.

After ten baskets the hoop starts to slide, and after twenty-five it moves faster and less predictably. Clean swishes pay a bonus, so the best scores come from consistent, controlled shots rather than hopeful long throws.
tips: Find one drag distance that sinks a shot and repeat it — consistency builds the streak.
Aim for nothing-but-net; rim shots that drop still keep the streak but miss the bonus.
When the hoop moves, shoot as it reaches the end of its path where it slows down.
Keyboard players can fine-tune power with the up and down arrows for repeatable shots.

faq.q: How long is a round of Hoop Streak?
faq.a: Each round lasts sixty seconds. Your score depends on how many baskets you make and how long you keep the streak going.

faq.q: Can I play with a keyboard?
faq.a: Yes. Left and right set the angle, up and down set the power, and Space shoots.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Bubble Blaster Arena
shortDescription: Aim, ricochet, clear the board. Pop a cluster and everything it was holding up falls with it — and a fresh row drops from the ceiling every eight shots.
howToPlay: Drag to aim and release to fire, or ←→ and Space. The dotted guide banks off the side walls exactly as the shot will. Three of a colour clears them; anything left with nothing above it drops, and dropped bubbles pay more than popped ones.
about: Bubble Blaster Arena is a bubble shooter where angles matter. Aim with the dotted guide, bank shots off the side walls, and match three or more of a colour to pop them.

Pop a group that was holding others up and everything beneath it falls — and dropped bubbles score more than popped ones. A new row lowers from the ceiling every eight shots, so clearing efficiently is the only way to stay ahead.
tips: Look for shots that cut a bubble's support — drops are worth more than pops.
Use wall bank shots to reach colours tucked behind others.
Count your shots: plan to clear space just before the next row drops every eighth shot.
Don't waste a shot on a single bubble if a nearby pair can make a three.

faq.q: How many bubbles do I need to match?
faq.a: Three or more of the same colour. Any bubbles left with nothing above them fall and score a bonus.

faq.q: When do new rows appear?
faq.a: A fresh row drops from the ceiling every eight shots.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Tank Duel Arena
shortDescription: One tank against one bot in a box full of walls that bounce your shells straight back at you. First to five hits takes the duel — then the bot gets better.
howToPlay: ←→ turns, ↑↓ drives, Space fires. On a phone, hold to drive towards your finger and release to shoot. The barrel points wherever the hull points — for the bot too, so if its barrel swings your way, move.
about: Tank Duel Arena is a one-on-one tank battle against a computer opponent. Drive around a walled arena, line up your barrel, and fire shells that ricochet off the walls — including straight back at you.

The first tank to land five hits wins the duel, and every victory makes the next bot sharper. Because both barrels point wherever the hull points, reading the bot's direction is as important as aiming your own.
tips: Use bank shots off walls to hit the bot from angles it is not covering.
Never fire straight at a nearby wall — your own shell can bounce back into you.
If the bot's barrel swings towards you, move sideways rather than backwards.
Keep moving between shots; a stationary tank is the easiest target.

faq.q: How do you win a duel?
faq.a: Land five hits on the bot before it lands five on you. Each win raises the bot's difficulty.

faq.q: Can my own shells hit me?
faq.a: Yes. Shells bounce off walls, so a careless shot can ricochet back into your tank.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.

title: Slope Runner X
shortDescription: Steer a rolling ball down an infinite neon slope. Two keys, no brakes, a road that keeps narrowing, and corners that push you towards the drop.
howToPlay: Use ← → or A and D to steer; on a phone, hold your finger left or right of centre. The ball rolls forward on its own and speeds up the further you go, so all you control is your line. Stay on the road, and pass close to the pylons for bonus points.
about: Slope Runner X sends a ball rolling down an endless neon slope. You only steer — the speed is out of your hands and keeps rising — while the road bends, narrows and pushes you towards the edge on every corner.

Pylons stand along the track and brushing past them close pays bonus points, so the best scores come from riding near danger rather than playing it safe. It is a classic unblocked slope-style game that loads instantly in a browser tab.
tips: Make small, early corrections — big swerves at high speed send you off the edge.
Drift towards the inside of a bend before it starts; corners push you outward.
Brush pylons for bonuses only when the road ahead is straight.
On touch screens, keep your finger close to the centre for finer steering.

faq.q: How do you control Slope Runner X?
faq.a: Steer with the left and right arrows or A and D. On a phone or tablet, hold your finger to the left or right of the screen's centre.

faq.q: How do I get a higher score?
faq.a: Survive longer and pass close to pylons — near misses pay bonus points on top of distance.

faq.q: Is it free and does it need a download?
faq.a: It is completely free and runs in any modern browser on a Chromebook, laptop, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install and no account to make.
